bib.title: A Methodology for Selecting and Composing Runtime Architecture Patterns for Production LLM Agents

legacy_report:
COVERAGE: Read everything: 26 pages, 78,761 chars, in full (body, Tables 1-7, discussion, related work, conclusion, disclaimer). References and the final 3 pages were only skimmed, since they are bibliography. No appendix with results. No extraction faults. No embedded instructions.

SOURCE: "A Methodology for Selecting and Composing Runtime Architecture Patterns for Production LLM Agents", Vasundra Srinivasan (independent researcher, AI Architect, "Stanford School of Engineering"), arXiv 2605.20173v2 [cs.AI], preprint, May 2026 (v2 dated 11 Aug 2026). Not peer reviewed.

CORE CLAIM: Name the "stochastic-deterministic boundary" (SDB) as the key primitive of production agent runtimes. It is a four-part contract: proposer (the LLM), verifier (a deterministic check), commit (the durable write), and reject signal (a typed response sent back to the proposer). Around it sit three concerns (Coordination, State, Control) and six patterns: P1 Hierarchical Delegation, P2 Scatter-Gather + Saga, P3 Event-Driven Sequencing, P5 Shared State Machine, P4 Supervisor + Gate, P6 Human in the Loop. A five-step selection method produces a six-line architecture decision record. Thesis: as per-call variance σ shrinks, architectural momentum µ is the main lever on reliability.

NUMBERS (all weak, author-classified):
- Audit of 5 OSS frameworks (swarm, AutoGPT, LangChain Agents, CrewAI, AutoGen): verifier-and-commit logic at 19 of 21 LLM-to-action call sites.
- Classification of 21 published post-mortems: 15 (71.4%) localize to the boundary, and 17 (81%) of the fixes strengthen it. The author did the classification (§8.2).
- Cited from Promptfoo (not original): GPT-4o to GPT-4.1 upgrade dropped prompt-injection resistance from 94% to 71% (23 points). The fix was an output classifier plus stricter tool gating.
- Cited issue: openai-agents-js #1104. Rejected tool calls were reported as status 'completed', so the model hallucinated success. The proposed fix was 'incomplete'.
- Reference app: 100 renewal scenarios from the IBM Telco Churn dataset, roughly 26.5% natural churn. It is a demo with no measured results.

ABLATION: None. §7 gives "what would go wrong if we picked differently" as argued prose, not experiments.

QUOTES:
- p.1: "The composition is the load-bearing engineering surface of every production agent and it does not yet have a name."
- §3 P4: "The gate denies. The audit log records. The supervisor restarts." Also: "Gate is a deterministic rule check. Policy decisions belong in code or in a fast rule engine."
- §3 P6: "Kill switch revokes a cancellation token in approximately one second." Four planes: kill switch, escalation, approval (synchronous wait under SLA, falls back to deny), throttling. Cancellation checks "at every tool boundary. Not just at workflow start."
- §5.1: "We present this as a metaphor, not as a derived model."
(Page numbers are approximate. The extraction did not mark pages, so I can give section names only.)

FIT TO NOTES: It is weak and off-centre for 04-execution-boundaries. The paper is a position and methodology paper with no experiments. It says nothing on sandboxes, hooks, OS isolation, the five protection layers or trust zones.
- Partial fit with note 04, as a citation only: the SDB verifier/commit/reject contract matches permission gates and hooks. P4 gate+supervisor, P6 kill switch, throttling (blast-radius caps) and saga compensation match rollback and the cost envelope. It could be cited under permission gates or rollback.
- Better fit: 02 anatomy, for the proposer/verifier/commit/reject contract and the pattern catalog (§3-4). The 08 maturity note fits for the "console-first" build sequence and the "defer a control plane but record why" rule.
- The replay-divergence and architectural-momentum material fits neither 04 nor 02 well. The momentum claim is unsupported.

LIMITS / NOT SHOWN:
- No benchmark, no deployed system, no measured reliability gain. The µ/σ model is a stylized metaphor with nothing fitted to data.
- The author built all five worked cases. §8.2 admits "Construction bias", no independent replication, and an author-made classification of failures.
- Thresholds (1 hour, 3 CAS retries) are conventions.
- Observed only on Claude Sonnet 4.6 and contemporary models. Better models may collapse the patterns.
- Replay divergence is asserted, not measured.
- Out of scope: RAG, evals, model selection, token budgets, prompts.
- Sandboxing and security isolation are not covered.
- A 5-framework, 21-site audit is a tiny sample.
- The audit and classification details live in the companion repo, not the paper.

BUILDS ON: Hewitt actor model [14]; Garcia-Molina and Salem sagas [11]; Lamport Paxos [20]; Armstrong Erlang supervision [2]; van der Aalst workflow nets [29]; Helland [13]; Kreps the log [19]; Corbett Spanner [9]. Closest LLM work: SagaLLM (Chang and Geng [7]) and ALAS [6]. Also NeMo Guardrails (Rebedea et al. [26]), GuardAgent [33], and the HITL survey (Wu et al. [32]). Years and venues are not in the extracted text; they are in the bibliography, which I did not read closely.

FIGURE CANDIDATE: Figure 1 (p.7), "The 3 by 6 catalog": three concerns by six patterns. A better option for note 04 is Table 2 (the six-line architecture decision record), but it is a table, not a figure.

RECOMMENDATION: At most "sharpens" in 04 (a one-line citation for the gate/kill-switch/throttle and deterministic-verifier point, flagged as a position paper with author-classified evidence), or a stronger fit in 02. Do not use its numbers as empirical support beyond the cited Promptfoo drop, which is second-hand.
